newsitem.title: UK: Man charged after N.Ireland rocket attack.
newsitem.headline: Man charged after N.Ireland rocket attack.

text.p: Northern Ireland police charged a man on Friday in connection with an Irish Republican Army (IRA) rocket attack on the province's main law courts in Belfast last Monday, security sources said.
The suspect, aged 27, was charged with conspiracy to murder and will appear in court on Saturday.
A policeman was slightly hurt when IRA guerrillas hit his security hut at the Courts of Justice complex last Monday with a missile fired from a passing car.

A number of men were detained for questioning afterwards. Security sources said earlier on Friday that at least six were being quizzed about the attack and about a double IRA carbomb blast that killed a soldier at British Army headquarters at Lisburn, south of Belfast, in October.
"We can confirm that a number of people are being questioned about serious crime in the Greater Belfast area," a spokesman for the Royal Ulster Constabulary police said.

The IRA, fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, disrupted peak-hour evening traffic in Belfast and nearby Lisburn on Friday with a spate of warnings of bombs at shopping areas and outside police stations.
They telephoned alerts to local news media saying devices had been left in vehicles at several locations.
As security forces checked them out, police said several had been established as hoaxes.
No devices had yet been found but several precautionary "controlled explosions" were set off by army bomb disposal officers called to suspect vehicles, security sources said.

A recent spate of attacks and botched raids by the IRA has prompted fears that Northern Ireland could slide back into the cycle of sectarian warfare that scarred it for 27 years until the IRA and its pro-British Protestant guerrilla foes declared twin truces more than two years ago.

Protestant "Loyalist" extremists have been blamed for two recent bomb attacks on leading Irish Republicans in Belfast and Londonderry, the province's second city, but Loyalist politicians insist the 26-month-old truce is still operating.

The IRA abandoned its ceasefire last February. Britain says the Republican guerrillas must declare a permanent end to violence before their political wing, Sinn Fein, can be given a seat in current multiparty talks on the province's future.
